Internal helper: c() of names in a variable list

Source: R/checks.R
dot-jst_expand_vars.Rd

Ruling R18 (Session 355; built Session 356): a variable list takes a c() of names, bare or quoted – jdesc(d, c(Age, Score)), jdesc(d, c("Age", "Score")) – as the tidyverse does, where it read "c(Age, Score) was not found". Each item becomes a variable of its own, in place, in the c()'s environment; a quoted item stays the string it was, which every list already reads as a name. Only a c() whose items are all names or strings is opened: a range (Age:Score), a helper, or an item computed inside the c() keeps the not-found stop, as decided. A named item (a misspelled argument, a condition) is left to .jst_check_named_variables().

Usage

.jst_expand_vars(quos)

Arguments

quos

The captured variable list, after any juse() prepend.

Value

The list with each such c() opened, class kept.
